 11/16 Game Preview: Magic at Celtics
 November 16, 2026 2:50 PM EST Provided by Field Level Media 
 Although Franz Wagner was held to 14 points when the Orlando Magic faced the Celtics earlier this month, he likely will be the focal point of his opponent when the teams meet in Boston on Monday night.
 Wagner has scored at least 30 points in each of his last four games. He had 35 points, 12 assists and nine rebounds in 36 minutes to help Orlando extend its winning streak to three games with a 107-99 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks on Friday night.
 "I think with the way we're playing, I see similar situations every game, over and over again," Wagner said. "I think with anything when you do that, for anybody it gets easier a little bit to make those plays with the speed of the game. I think that's been it. We're playing more consistent on offense, and I think that helps everybody with their decision-making."
 Wagner is averaging 24.4 points, 8.3 assists and 6.8 rebounds for a team that still is without injured star Paolo Banchero (right ankle sprain).
 "He's a killer," teammate Desmond Bane said about Wagner, 25, a sixth-year forward out of Michigan. "I was on the court with him, and I had to ask him that in the fourth quarter, 'Are you a killer?' And he's like, 'Yeah, I'm a killer.' He is. He does it on both ends of the floor.
 "... Play after play, whether he's scoring, assisting, using his voice in the timeouts -- I think that's something that he's grown at a lot this season, just leadership. His focus is there.
 "He's a competitive guy that wants to win, wants to play the right way and he's being rewarded for all the work that he's put in."
 Initially, it looked as if Orlando would be catching a break by playing Boston on the second night of a back-to-back set, but the Celtics met little resistance during their 131-94 victory over the Dallas Mavericks on Sunday. Boston, which has won six straight games, had a 33-point lead after one quarter and removed its starters at the end of the third.
 Jayson Tatum, who is averaging a team-high 26.8 points per game, scored 32 points in 30 minutes against the Mavericks. He's the only Boston player who played more than 25 minutes.
 Jordan Walsh, who spent much of Sunday's game defending Dallas' Cooper Flagg, likely will be assigned to Wagner on Monday.
 "Jordan's continuing to develop the mindset that we need him to have against great players," Boston coach Joe Mazzulla said. "And a great team has to have a group of guys that they can rely on to make it difficult for the team's best player every single day. ... Jordan's on that list."
 Boston had 10 players make at least one 3-pointer during Sunday's win. The Celtics sank 23 of 55 (41.8%) shots from 3-point range.
 "Guarding them, the 3-point shooting is something that stands out," Orlando coach Sean Sweeney said. "Their crash rate -- the amount that they crash (the glass). ... Tatum, (we've) got to do a better job guarding him without fouling. ... As well as guys like Paul George and Payton Pritchard, who are really, really efficient right now."
 --Field Level Media
